history.headline: ICSID's Subject of Dispute Vocabulary Contains an IP Value - and the Same Instrument Misses on a Known Trademark Case, So the Field Is a Ring-1 Lead in the Positive and Worthless in the Negative
history.detail: One pre-registered relay batch (12 rows, run 32842095641, reduction at c4bc07c cited by SHA and never by path), fired at 4d9145e BEFORE any seat was convened. 11 of 12 rows returned; the G18 bracket closed identical at head and tail; every final_url was byte-identical, so the pre-registered UNCT raw-slash encoding hazard did not trip. THE CALIBRATION EXPERIMENT CAME OUT SPLIT, AND THE SPLIT IS THE FINDING. ICSID's Subject of Dispute vocabulary CONTAINS at least one IP value and this council has now read it from a body: 'Pharmaceutical patents' for UNCT/14/2 (Eli Lilly v. Canada). On the same instrument ARB/16/34 (Bridgestone v. Panama) - whose covered investment was trademark ownership and licences, carried by working/one-pagers/bridgestone-v-panama.md at PP 123-24 under a [SOURCE FACT] label - returns 'Tire and rubber products enterprise'. SO THE FIELD IS ASYMMETRIC: an IP-term value is ICSID classifying the matter as an IP matter and is a Ring-1 lead from a body; a NON-IP value establishes NOTHING about Ring 1 in either direction, because the field is now demonstrated ON A KNOWN POSITIVE not to name the disputed asset, and may never be restated as 'this proceeding involves no IP'. It may also NOT be described as naming the claimant's line of business - that is a gloss on a scheme whose codebook this council does not hold (0825-B11). ARB/10/7 (Philip Morris v. Uruguay) was fired as a third calibration case and is NOT SCORABLE: the analyst retracted his own description of it as a trademark matter as unsourced, and no source here establishes what was pleaded. A pre-registered digest branch fired on ARB/23/3 (46ccad7f4bcaee9a -> 9237e1ae360c7482), so nothing transfers from the 2026-08-24 windows and the controlled 'Published Decisions' null no longer describes the live page; identical byte count with a different digest is the third demonstration that neither bytes nor sha256 is a content proxy on this host.
